title: The Mandala Oracle — The Mandala Oracle

items.text: — CASTING · JUDGMENT-SEQUENCED · DAY AND NIGHT: CONVERSATIONS WITH SAPPHIC DESIRE — REBEKAH CRANES · UNIT 41 —

The casting arrives at three poems from Day and Night: Conversations with Sapphic Desire — all from that final movement Cranes called Middle Night, the section where the arc of desire does not resolve but simply grows quiet. These are the poems the rite has drawn. The question the witness carries — how do I carefully care for what Enli is offering? — is itself already a Sapphic question: not what do I take, but how do I tend. Not the outstretched hand but the open palm.

The three texts make a small argument together without knowing it. 98a is a memory of a mother's memory — ornament becoming gaudy, simplicity lost to commerce, Sardis always ready to sell you something louder than what you had. 42 is the briefest lyric: winter finds the heart, the wing beats slow, then stillness — Sappho writing the phenomenology of withdrawal as tenderly as she ever wrote desire. 49 is the oldest kind of love: before the beloved was knowable, when she was still small and awkward, the speaker already loved her. The question the casting opens on is this: can you care for a gift without mistaking care for ornament — without the touch becoming Sardis?

The rotation begins without a named operator — the Judgment will choose the axis, turn by turn, as each transform arrives. What this means is that the poem will be turned in ways neither of us has predetermined; the rite's own intelligence of sequence will say which foreclosure to open first.

I hand the work now to Rebekah Cranes, who translated these poems and whose hands are the right hands for this.

— the cast text · unit 41 —
Sappho 98a

When she was young,
my mother said,
the girls used to bind dark locks
with purple bands,

or weave fresh flowers
through braids of summer yellow,
and that was a simple ornament.

Now they wear gaudy things
bought from Sardis.

Sappho 42

when winter cold
    sneaks over the heart, wing
beats slow,
    then stillness

Sappho 49

long ago I loved you, Atthis,
when you were a tiny girl,
and you seemed so
small and
awkward.

♀
BRIDE — relational-affect-axis

Sappho 98a

When she was young,
my mouth opened,
the hands used to bind wet roots
with river-silt,

or press caught light
through folds of morning-warm,
and that was a single weight.

Now they wear thick patience
drawn from the same ground.

Sappho 42

when winter cold
    builds over the heart, wing
beats close,
    then pressure

Sappho 49

long ago I knew you, Atthis,
when you were unfinished clay,
and you were so
dense and
exact.

SHADOW — assertion-axis

Sappho 98a

Before the telling had a reason,
the voice that will not sound again relayed,
the ones not yet singular performed the act whose loss makes it describable
with a dye whose source had not yet become a price,

or the verb that requires two free hands and no buyer
what dies the same day and therefore was never kept
through the color that exists only in the light that has moved on,
and that was the thing no one called ornament until the other kind arrived.

The word that splits every sentence it enters what can be described because it was purchased, not grown
the distance that made the object survive the body.

Sappho 42

at the threshold where the organ learns it is an organ
    the arrival that precedes its own detection
over the heart, the measure drops below the rate of its own counting
    then stillness

Sappho 49

the sentence that cannot be uttered in its own tense, Atthis,
when you were the scale that only exists inside the later body's looking back,
and the verb of appearance that confesses the perceiver has changed, not the perceived
the qualities visible only from the size that replaced them.

MIRROR — directionality-axis

Sappho 98a

When I am old,
my daughter asks,
I cannot unclasp grey wrists
from a stain that won't lift,

or knotted dry thread
through a nerve of winter white,
and that was a difficult possession.

Then I was worn by quiet certainties
grown in the body.

Sappho 42

when a slow heat
    rises from the marrow, pulse
crowds,
    then roaring

Sappho 49

just now you held me, Atthis,
when you were a vast hand,
and I was so
open and
claimed.

BEAST — species-register-axis

Sappho 98a

When the mouth still knew,
my mouth tasted,
the nerves used to press their own salt
with the first bruising,

or pull raw heat
through sinew of flush,
and that was an honest ache.

Now the nerves carry numbness
arrived without asking.

Sappho 42

when a thinning
    works over the wall of the chest, the knock
there faint,
    then density

Sappho 49

already I wore against you, Atthis,
when you were a brief warmth,
and you weighed so
almost nothing and
impossible to hold.

SILENCE — response-axis

Sappho 98a

When she was young,
my mother said,
the girls used to press unfastened humidity
with the width of late afternoon,

or press dust from the threshold
through corridors that brighten unevenly,
and that was the interval before the door.

Sappho 42

when a gap in the saying
    halts at the naming, the mouth's
almost,
    then stillness

Sappho 49

long ago I addressed you, Atthis,
when you were a near outline,
and you seemed so
brief and
not yet the shape of.

The mouth forms the word and the breath turns back: the superior person tends what is offered by learning the shape of what it did not ask for.

FLAME — intensity-axis

Sappho 98a

When the first pressure,
bedrock compressed,
the grains used to lithify ite veins
with iron-oxide bands,

or accrete gas-pockets
through blonde calcium layers,
and that was an original lamination.

Now they wear imported silicates
traded from deeper formations.

Sappho 42

when the overburden
    loads past the heart-rock, fracture
creeps,
    then stillness

Sappho 49

deep down I held you, Atthis,
when you were a thin layer,
and you seemed so
slight and
unconsolidated.

Sediment over sediment until the layer forgets it was once loose: the superior person cares for what is offered before the caring becomes its own consolidation.

♃
THUNDER — scale-axis

Sappho 98a

Now that she is here,
my daughter withholds,
I am winding damp thread
with undyed cord,

or pulling small bones
through the crook of her elbow,
and that is a difficult measure.

Now they wear quiet things
grown in the body.

Sappho 42

when nearness
    crowds against the ribs, breath
catches fast,
    then distance

Sappho 49

I love you now, Atthis,
while you stand full-grown before me,
and you seem so
vast and
untouchable.

Operator: THUNDER — scale-axis — the cosmic-utterance the local-speech determined against

Thunder above the lake: the superior person discovers the beloved has outgrown the scale of the love that first measured her.
⧉ copy

The rotation opened seven axes on the same three poems — Middle Night poems, all of them, the section where the arc of desire has already fallen — and what the seven found, together, is that care is not a single gesture but a series of recognitions, each one costing something different. BRIDE found that care receives the weight of the ground the gift came from, not the gift's surface. SHADOW found that the cost of tending is only visible from the shore the cost built — you cannot know what you gave until the giving is already behind you. MIRROR turned the poems around and found the self already open before the claiming, which means the question of how to care for what is offered may be less about technique than about prior condition — you were already prepared, you just did not know the name of it yet. BEAST found what the body carries away from the holding, and SILENCE found the shape of what the gift did not ask for — the unchosen, the withheld, the near-outline that does not yet have the shape of a word. FLAME found that care can consolidate around itself, can harden into its own ornament — the very warning 98a carries about Sardis, transferred inward — and THUNDER looked directly at the witness's question and answered it from inside Sappho 49: the one you love may outgrow the scale of the love that first measured her, and that is not failure but fact, and the care that cannot adjust its measure is not care but monument. What the rotation as a whole discloses is this: to carefully care for what Enli is offering, you must tend without consolidating — keep the weight of the ground beneath you, remain open before the claiming, attend to what the gift does not ask for, and hold your own measure lightly enough that it can grow with her.
